problem_type: MCP semantic media journey contract regression
symptom: The real C-L2 journey loses the reason for a declined canvas plan, shows only reference counts on the paid challenge, returns no reviewable poster for a video artifact, and leaves export-execution.json without the build identity needed for reconciliation.
direct_cause: The shared MCP/result boundaries projected cancellation and gate data with reduced shapes; video output materialization did not persist provider-owned poster media; and the export receipt writer persisted runtime output without a buildSha field.
class_root: Durable MCP and export receipts were assembled independently from the underlying production contracts, so fields required to explain a user decision, review a media artifact, or reconcile an export were not carried through the shared projection/materialization boundaries.
affected_population: MCP clients declining a batch canvas plan
MCP clients approving multi-shot generation with reference media
MCP clients reviewing generated video artifacts
Operators reconciling export outputs across builds
entry_points: production artifact projection and MCP thumbnail enrichment
generality_proof: Any future semantic MCP result or durable export/media receipt assembled from these shared boundaries inherits the same field-preservation requirement; callers do not need a vendor-specific branch.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Preserve safe structured MCP results and notification/confirmation outcomes.
Turn provider outputs into validated project-owned media receipts.
Expose scoped artifact paths and signed previews.
Persist the export execution reconciliation receipt.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The response carries reason=declined and remains cancelled without ids.
Each shot carries safe referenceMedia identities when candidate references exist.
Provider thumbnailUrl is fetched and persisted as a project-owned poster.
Video artifacts expose poster as a thumbnail-first signed preview.
The fixture supplies the stable semantic shot bindings required for the same production materialization and export journey without changing the provider or payment seam.
The receipt includes a non-empty buildSha for cross-build reconciliation.

internal_only_reason: These are Nomi-owned projection, materialization, and receipt invariants; no external provider documentation can define which safe fields must remain available to an MCP client or an export reconciler.
invariants: A declined canvas plan returns cancelled=true with a typed reason and never creates nodes.
A multi-shot paid challenge projects safe reference asset identities per shot, never local paths or provider URLs.
A completed video provider output with a poster URL persists a local poster and exposes it as the artifact poster/preview.
Every persisted export execution receipt includes a non-empty buildSha.

recurrence.reason: The same loss-of-contract pattern affects multiple independent MCP and durable-receipt consumers; shared projections and materialization are the earliest common boundaries.
same_class_scan: Scanned all MCP result builders and widget-bound nomiRunData paths; nomi_canvas_edit, nomi_operation_gate, nomi_read artifact and run_events are the active C-L2 consumers.

Scanned all GenerationProviderOutput producers and consumers; APIMart extraction and generationOutputMaterializer are the shared media path, while legacy production fixture output already carries poster data and remains not-affected.
Scanned export receipt writers; exportJobs.ts is the sole export-execution.json writer, and existing export verification reads the same job directory.
Checked the old J-MCP1 and production/draft journeys; only J-MCP1 is retired, while shared harness consumers remain in scope and are not-affected.

prevention.invariant: The field needed for a user decision, media review, or build reconciliation is present at the first shared boundary and survives the structured MCP projection.
prevention.failure_mode: A future caller adds a reduced result shape or bypasses poster/receipt persistence.
prevention.strategy: derive safe fields from canonical candidate/output/receipt data and test both positive and negative paths.

legacy_paths.rationale: J-MCP1 is replaced by the C7-C12 lane; shared harness consumers remain and are explicitly audited rather than removed.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No dependency is added or retained; the fixture uses the repository's existing Electron, ffmpeg, and HTTP runtime dependencies.

migration: No user data migration. Existing video artifacts without a poster remain readable; new semantic provider video outputs materialize a poster when the provider returns one. Existing export receipts remain readable and new receipts carry buildSha.
residual_risks: A provider that returns no poster URL still has no MCP image block; the client receives the playable artifact preview and can open it in Nomi.
CI window managers may minimize Electron; screenshot evidence therefore asserts file existence and non-zero dimensions only.
